strengths: Addresses a practically important problem of LRM inefficiency with clear motivation and strong empirical results (35% cost reduction without performance loss)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 math datasets with thorough ablation studies demonstrating component effectiveness
Well-motivated combination of complementary techniques (reflection model for efficiency, reflection reward for performance preservation) with clear analysis of their distinct contributions
Insightful analysis showing overthinking is problem-specific (higher on easy problems, lower on hard problems) with principled mitigation strategy
Clear presentation of methodology with detailed experimental setup, hyperparameters, and prompts supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Evaluation scope severely limited to single distilled 7B model with no validation on larger models, from-scratch pretrained models, or non-math domains, raising significant generalization concerns
Dependency on external 32B LLM (Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct) for initial overthinking detection creates practical limitations and undermines efficiency claims

Overthinking detection and reflection reward rely on simplistic heuristics (keyword matching, gold answer requirement) with no comparison to alternative approaches; keywords may appear in non-reflective contexts
Experimental setup bias: training data filtered to only questions answerable in 4 samples (40k→30k); GRPO RLen baseline performs suspiciously poorly, raising hyperparameter fairness questions

Limited novelty in individual components (LLM-based detection, keyword rewards, sequential revision are each relatively standard); contribution is primarily in combination which is somewhat incremental
No error analysis or qualitative comparison of reasoning patterns; reflection reward based on keyword density cannot fully capture complex reflection phenomenon
Computational overhead (~10% additional cost) and reliance on reflection model during inference not fully quantified; training requires significant GPU resources (3× A800 80G for 120 hours)
Missing experiments on generalization: different model scales/architectures, non-math reasoning domains, and applicability without 32B external model during training

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical overthinking efficiency in LRMs with clear motivation (Figure 1)
Thorough experimental evaluation across 5 math datasets with extensive baselines and 8k/16k budgets
Strong empirical results: 36% token reduction without accuracy degradation, with good analysis of how reflection is preserved on hard problems
Comprehensive ablation studies validating both reflection model and reward components
Good insights on training dynamics and appropriate reflection frequency adaptation across problem difficulties
Reproducibility: detailed appendices with prompts, hyperparameters, and promised code release
Practical approach suitable for online deployment vs. expensive offline data generation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: overthinking detection is straightforward (first correct answer), reflection model uses standard SFT, reflection reward uses simple keyword heuristics; contribution is primarily engineering combination
Significant practical overhead: requires training auxiliary 7B model (+50% training time), sequential revision causes parallelism bottlenecks (~10% additional cost), complex hyperparameter tuning

Scope limitations: main results restricted to math reasoning (5 datasets); general QA results (Appendix B.3) show modest improvements suggesting limited generalization; only validated on distilled 7B models, not pre-trained
Weak reflection detection: 32B distillation has 17% failure rate, answer-mention-based detection is noisy and language-specific, cannot 'guarantee complete elimination of overthinking'

Reflection reward design is heuristic-based and brittle: language-specific keywords ('wait', 'but', 'check', 'alternatively') may not capture all reflection types; quantile D₀.₂ selection lacks principled justification

Missing experimental rigor: no error bars/confidence intervals, no variance analysis across runs, small test sets (Aime24: 48 samples), GRPO RLen baseline shows suspicious ~6% accuracy collapse unexplained

Incomplete analysis: no failure case discussion, no semantic equivalence verification of revisions, no cost-benefit analysis of training overhead, limited Gen8 comparison justifying sequential over parallel sampling
